correctness.rationale: The finite-dimensional positive-path Lie algebra is the commutator of an associative radical, so satisfies Jacobi over every field. Direct tensor decomposition gives the full derived and third lower-central subspaces; commuting with the former forces both outer arrow components to vanish because all multiplicities are positive and tensoring with a nonzero vector is injective. Thus the intrinsic quotient centralizer dimension is s, while the first and third graded dimensions give r+t and rst; recovering integer r,t follows. Reversal with a global minus sign supplies all sufficiency cases, including characteristic two. The rigorous argument covers every field and all positive triples. A separate exact modular checker reproduced every invariant in 81 small cases; such finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A complete if-and-only-if classification of a natural unbounded family of three-step nilpotent Lie algebras is an intrinsic structural statement, not a routine isolated count or mere reversal. It strengthens a recent dimension-at-most-ten classification and shows in an infinite family that matching full lower-central graded dimensions does not classify these Lie algebras. The derived-centralizer quotient provides a reusable structural distinguishing invariant.
